acceptance_criteria: First-run absence is a distinct tested uninitialized state rather than an error or observed empty registry.
Corrupt JSON, non-array content, invalid members, permission failure, and generic read failure produce typed non-observed results.
Evaluation, API, and console cannot translate a non-observed result into no active mutes or a proven unsilenced instance.
Adding or removing while the registry is unavailable or invalid fails without changing destination bytes or creating a replacement registry.
Valid mutations preserve the private atomic-publication guarantees already merged from #2338.
Last-known-good use is explicitly bounded by snapshot freshness and each rule's expiry, and recovery requires a fresh successful read.
API and Settings distinguish loading, uninitialized, unavailable, stale, valid empty, and observed nonempty states.
Repeated failures produce one bounded onset and one recovery transition without paths, raw errors, rule content, identities, or topology.
Public documentation distinguishes authorized reset from accidental loss or corruption of active suppression state.
blast_radius: Planned-maintenance suppression, alert evaluation, registry repair evidence, silence API truth, Settings operator controls, recovery signaling, and public durability guidance for the active silence artifact.
evidence_summary: All decisive product and focused-test blobs are byte-identical between the prior pin and 9a1bd7b3d3c529b276c1ad764d2c312d7f3abfc3. The public-surface document changed only in unrelated Git-guard rows, and its silence-registry contract remains byte-for-byte unchanged. Exact-main silence-manager source returns the same empty array for first-run absence, corrupt JSON, non-array content, and other read failure, validates only that the document is an array, and casts every member. Evaluation then returns false, listing returns empty, and addSilence filters that fallback and atomically publishes a new registry. GET always returns HTTP 200 with a silences array, while Settings consumes only data and maps a missing response to No active mutes. Public documentation calls the active suppression registry safe to delete. Nineteen write-free source assertions reproduced those seams. The Settings, manager, and route suites passed 44 of 44 tests at the new exact main; they establish current behavior but do not include the removed corrupt-overwrite canary. One historical complete nested capture covered 237 open issues, all 39 open pull requests, all changed-file and closing-reference pages, and 37 labels. A required second capture failed closed on top-level inventory drift, so no stable complete-estate claim is made. The historical capture and direct searches found no owner; publication still requires the declared fresh estate rescan.
falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The issue is falsified if every non-valid load state is distinguishable, mutation requires a current validated read, and corrupt bytes remain unchanged under ordinary add or remove. Exact source shows the opposite control flow. The decisive Settings, manager, and route suites passed 44 of 44 at the new exact main, but the issue's removed corrupt-overwrite falsifier was not recreated in this record-only lane and remains an explicit implementation-time obligation.
impact: A storage incident can silently disable all mutes, affirm an empty registry, and let an ordinary add overwrite recoverable suppression state, producing alert storms and destroying evidence.
lead_verification_obligations: Re-read issue #2533 immediately before publication and reject the record if its state, node identity, title, labels, update time, or exact body hash changed.
Reconfirm SSH origin, tracking main, remote main, and API main agreement before integration.
Repeat two complete nested estate captures and require exact equality before relying on PR ownership or overlap completeness.
Run the manager and route suites plus the corrupt-registry byte-preservation falsifier in an isolated mutable harness before completion.
Preserve #2338 atomic publication, reject ordinary mutation from unavailable or invalid state, and keep explicit repair or reset separately authorized and audited.
Coordinate taxonomy with #2447 and metadata-only logging with #2164 and #2517 without publishing paths, raw errors, rules, actors, or instance identities.
Use git range-diff or cherry comparison before treating open PR #2308 as superseded or retiring its preservation branch.
